questions.explain: Never UPDATE in place — the original is part of the audit trail. Freeze the old content as a version in message_versions, update the message, and mark downstream assistant messages stale since they were generated from the old content.
options: Append a new version: freeze old content in message_versions, update the message, mark downstream assistant messages stale
questions.q: How are user message edits stored?

questions.explain: Regenerations create siblings sharing a branch_group_id with one active member; the UI shows a ← → carousel; inactive siblings persist as preference data (chosen vs rejected) for training.
options: Sibling branches with one active member — inactive siblings are preference data for training

questions.explain: Forks are new conversations sharing history by reference (forked_from_conversation_id, forked_at_message_id) — no copying; copy-on-write via version chains handles divergence, and deletes must respect surviving forks.
options: Copy all messages to a new conversation
Fork by reference: new conversation row sharing history up to the fork point, divergence via version chains

questions.explain: Bound growth: keep the active sibling plus the N most recent inactive ones, align edit retention with the audit policy, and clean up abandoned forks (no activity in 90 days, never shared) with user notice.
options: Sibling limits, audit-aligned edit retention, and abandoned-fork cleanup
questions.q: How is version history kept from growing unbounded?

questions.explain: Three patterns: inline edit affordance (hover shows 'edited', click opens old-vs-new diff), sibling carousel (← 2/4 → with model and token cost per sibling), and a fork graph for power users — progressive disclosure, never cluttering the main view.
options: Inline edit diffs, sibling carousels, and fork graphs — progressive disclosure on demand
Only show the active version ever
